note: Exam Mode data (prompt EM1). Blocks are the backbone (decisions 18-19). Packs hold questions; C1 is the core combination (input + loop + selection + update + output). Approved by Theo 24-25 Nov 2026. testAnswers are the marker's gate: it must agree on at least 95% of mark points per question, and every total must match.

blocks.name: Input and store a value
mistakes: assignment the wrong way round: input("…") = passA (2025 6(a)(i))
printing when asked to store (ER 2024)
changing a given identifier, e.g. word 1 for word1 (ER 2024)
input used as a variable name

blocks.name: Selection with one condition
mistakes: comparing to a word without quotes (== yes)
= instead of == (penalised once)
both outputs printed

blocks.name: Two conditions (AND/OR) and inclusive ranges
mistakes: num >= 1 AND <= 100: variable not repeated (ER 2024, ER 2025)
num > 1 AND num < 100 shuts out the boundaries (ER 2025)
≥ or => instead of >= (ER 2024)

blocks.name: Count-controlled loop
cuePhrases: until the quantity of numbers the user input has been entered
mistakes: repeating the calculation without a new input each time (2022 4(c))
a while loop whose counter never changes

blocks.name: Loop over an array, counter as index
mistakes: not using the loop counter as the index (ER 2024: the hardest mark)
inventing a 2D index for a 1D array (ER 2024)
for x in list then list[x] (ER 2024)
starting at index 1 (2022 5(d), 2023 2(b))

blocks.name: Running total, count or update a variable
mistakes: total = 0 inside the loop (2022 5(d))
print(total + x) never changes total
updating even when the booking failed (ER 2025)

blocks.name: Define a subprogram (function or procedure)
blocks.cue: takes … as a parameter and returns …
cuePhrases: Create/Write a function, X(), that takes … as a parameter
mistakes: no parameter, or input() overwriting it (ER 2024, ER 2025)
print instead of return (ER 2025)
code outside the function body

blocks.name: Condition-controlled loop
cuePhrases: repeat continually until the user enters 0
repeat the steps until there are no … left
mistakes: input only before the loop, so it repeats forever (2022 5(e))
resetting the variable inside the loop (2025 6(e))
"a while loop repeats until the condition is True" (ER 2025)
while x > 0 when the stop value is 0 (2022 5(e))

blocks.name: Call a subprogram and use its result
cuePhrases: stores the result in the variable Y
mistakes: redefining the function instead of calling it (ER 2025)
== for assignment
a text argument without quotes

blocks.name: String handling
blocks.cue: the first … letters / … characters in length
mistakes: comma instead of + to join (ER 2024)
printing instead of storing (ER 2024)
string methods combined with casting (ER 2024)

blocks.name: Output a message with a variable
cuePhrases: outputs "…" and then the content of the variable
mistakes: the variable inside the quotes (ER 2025)

blocks.name: Arithmetic: MOD, DIV, ^, average
blocks.cue: remainder / average / to the power of
mistakes: average worked out inside the loop
MOD and DIV swapped
x for multiply (not accepted in Section B)

blocks.name: 2D arrays
mistakes: row and column swapped
adding text without casting
a single index on a 2D array

blocks.name: Casting
cuePhrases: must be converted to a string
takes the PIN as input as a string
mistakes: generic definition where context is asked for (2025 4(b))
int() on text with a decimal point

blocks.name: Reading and writing files
cuePhrases: read … from the external text file
write these inputs to the … text file
stores the string of data to the text file
mistakes: overwriting the procedure's parameters with input()
typing the file name instead of using the parameter (2023 6(e))
not knowing the ERL file statements

blocks.name: Highest or lowest
mistakes: over-complicated array solutions instead of a running highest (ER 2024)

questions.title: Gaming café
questions.stem: A gaming café records how long each gamer plays.
bullets: asks the user to enter the number of minutes a gamer played
adds the minutes to a running total
outputs the total number of minutes.
questions.sayItSimply: Ask how many minutes someone played. Add it to a total. Keep asking until they type 0. Then show the total.
questions.answerFormat: Write an algorithm: code, pseudocode or a flowchart all get marks on paper. In Exam Mode you answer in Python.
questions.modelPython:
total = 0
minutes = int(input("Enter minutes played (0 to stop): "))
while minutes != 0:
    total = total + minutes
    minutes = int(input("Enter minutes played (0 to stop): "))
print("Total minutes played:", total)
questions.modelERL:
total = 0
minutes = input("Enter minutes played (0 to stop)")
while minutes != 0
    total = total + minutes
    minutes = input("Enter minutes played (0 to stop)")
endwhile
print("Total minutes played: " + str(total))

markPoints.text: Inputs the minutes and stores them
markPoints.feedback: You did not ask for the minutes. Write minutes = int(input("Enter minutes: ")).

markPoints.text: Adds the minutes to the total (total = total + minutes)
markPoints.feedback: Your total never changes. Inside the loop, write total = total + minutes.

markPoints.text: Repeats the input and the adding until 0 is entered
markPoints.feedback: Your program does not keep asking until 0. Put the input and the adding inside while minutes != 0:, and ask for the minutes again at the end of the loop.

markPoints.text: Outputs the total once, after the loop
markPoints.feedback: Show the total once, after the loop. Write print(total) with no indent, below the loop.

guidance: Don't penalise a missing total = 0 at the start; total = 0 inside the loop loses BP2.

questions.title: Strike Zone bowling
questions.rider: You must use either: OCR Exam Reference Language, or a high-level programming language that you have studied.
questions.stem: Strike Zone is a bowling alley. A game costs £5.00. Members pay £3.50 per game.
bullets: take as input the number of games a customer wants to play and whether they are a member
calculate and output the price for that customer
repeat until the user enters 0 games.
questions.sayItSimply: Ask how many games, and whether they're a member. Members pay £3.50 a game. Everyone else pays £5. Show the price. Keep doing this until someone types 0 games.
questions.answerFormat: Code only: pseudocode in English or a flowchart gets no marks here.
questions.modelERL:
games = input("Enter number of games (0 to stop)")
while games != 0
    member = input("Are you a member? (yes/no)")
    if member == "yes" then
        price = games * 3.50
    else
        price = games * 5
    endif
    print("Price: £" + str(price))
    games = input("Enter number of games (0 to stop)")
endwhile

tests.note: -1 must not stop the loop (it is not 0)
one member; used for BP3 even if the loop is wrong
one non-member; used for BP4 even if the loop is wrong

markPoints.text: Inputs the number of games and whether they're a member (two separate inputs), and stores them
markPoints.feedback: You need two inputs. Write games = int(input("How many games? ")) and member = input("Member? yes/no: ").
You did not check if they are a member. Write if member == "yes":.

markPoints.text: …correctly calculates and outputs the price for a member (games * 3.50)
markPoints.feedback: Members pay £3.50 a game. Under the if, write price = games * 3.50 and print(price).

markPoints.text: …correctly calculates and outputs the price for a non-member (games * 5)
markPoints.feedback: Non-members pay £5 a game. Under else:, write price = games * 5 and print(price).
Your program only does one customer. Put the inputs, the if and the print inside a loop.

markPoints.text: …until 0 games is entered, asking for new inputs each time
markPoints.feedback: Your loop must stop only when 0 is typed, and ask again each time. Write while games != 0: and ask for games again at the end of the loop.

guidance: Inputs before the loop and again at its end is fine.
Do not accept while games > 0 for BP6.
Repeating the calculation without new inputs gets no BP5 or BP6.
Don't penalise a 0 or blank output when the loop ends.
Missing quotes round "yes": penalise once, then follow through.
Missing int(): no marks lost; add the note.

else:
    price = games * 5
print(price)

member == yes without quotes: penalise once on BP3 (judgement call, approved)
No int(): full marks plus the int() note
for i in range(10): BP5 yes, BP6 no (judgement call, approved)

questions.title: Riverside quiz league
questions.rider: You must use either: OCR Exam Reference Language, or a high-level programming language that you have studied.
questions.stem: The Riverside quiz league records the score of each team in a round.
bullets: asks the user to enter a team name, or "stop" to finish
if a team name is entered, asks for that team's score
counts how many teams were entered and totals their scores
outputs the number of teams and the average score.
questions.sayItSimply: Ask for a team name. If it isn't "stop", ask for their score. Keep going until someone types stop. Count the teams and add up the scores. At the end, show how many teams there were and their average score.
questions.answerFormat: Code only: pseudocode in English or a flowchart gets no marks here.
questions.modelPython:
count = 0
total = 0
team = input("Enter a team name, or stop to finish: ")
while team != "stop":
    score = int(input("Enter the team's score: "))
    count = count + 1
    total = total + score
    team = input("Enter a team name, or stop to finish: ")
print("Teams entered:", count)
print("Average score:", total / count)
questions.modelERL:
count = 0
total = 0
team = input("Enter a team name, or stop to finish")
while team != "stop"
    score = input("Enter the team's score")
    count = count + 1
    total = total + score
    team = input("Enter a team name, or stop to finish")
endwhile
print("Teams entered: " + str(count))
print("Average score: " + str(total / count))

markPoints.text: Inputs a team name and stores it
markPoints.feedback: You did not ask for a team name. Write team = input("Team name, or stop: ").
Your program only takes one team. Put the score input and the adding inside a while loop.

markPoints.text: …until "stop" is entered, asking for a new team name each time
markPoints.feedback: Your loop must stop when "stop" is typed. Write while team != "stop":, and ask for the next team at the end of the loop.

markPoints.text: Asks for the score only when the name is not "stop"
markPoints.feedback: You asked for a score after "stop" was typed. Check the name first. Ask for the score inside the loop, before asking for the next name.

markPoints.text: Counts the teams and totals the scores inside the loop
markPoints.feedback: Count and total inside the loop. Write count = count + 1 and total = total + score. Set both to 0 before the loop.

markPoints.text: Outputs the count and the average (total / count) after the loop
markPoints.feedback: Show the results once, after the loop. Write print(count) and print(total / count) with no indent.

guidance: "stop" must be compared as text in quotes; team != stop is penalised once, then follow through.
Don't penalise a missing count = 0 or total = 0 before the loop; setting either inside the loop loses BP5.
Ignore division by zero if "stop" is typed first.
